chapter_title: The Catechumen asks the Apostle: will Rest come ab

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
When anyone who is being formed for heaven turns in full trust toward the good of love and asks for it, the very asking is already a true movement of the heart; and because the Divine is compassion itself, that turning is received. If the turning is chiefly for one’s own restoration, it is received according to that need; and if it is chiefly for another’s restoration, it is likewise received, because love looks beyond self and therefore more fully accords with heaven.

This way of asking has existed from the earliest ordering of spiritual life, when the first recipients of heavenly intelligence turned themselves toward the Divine Source and sought aid; and what they sought was granted.

The manner of that ancient asking can be taught: how the earliest states of ordered life sought from the Divine, and how reception is formed when the aim is the right ordering of all things.

The primary wisdom that proceeds from Divine love turned itself wholly to the First Divine, and from affection ascribed all good and all power to that Source. From this humility and love it sought restoring influx and a determinate provision of help, and it received a great communication of strength together with many operative faculties that attend wisdom conjoined to love.

That wisdom sought help for the primal good in a person, because that good had gone forth into ultimates and immersed itself there, becoming remote from its own higher life. It had relinquished itself into distress and entered combat in the lowest degree where destruction, grief, and weakening prevail—within states of falsity and evil, within the deepest fears, amid the compulsions and cravings of hellish persuasions.

For the case was as an inmost governing good beset on every side by contraries. Therefore wisdom, in its turning to the First Divine, sought that a protecting and rescuing power might be sent—an aid for the Divine good held in distress.

This intercession was received into the Divine presence; and the Divine provided what was sought: a great rescuing influx, the living operation of Divine truth that gives relief. Then wisdom and that living operation advanced in power to the outmost limits of the spiritual domain, and from there raised the embattled good out of the struggle in which it had been held.

That delivered good returned as a gift to wisdom; yet it had been made remote, because opposing forces had pressed it into severe distress and weakened it in states devoid of good.

But the living operation of Divine truth took hold of it, liberated it, restored it to order, and gave it tranquility in a state of peace and protection. This relief was according to the united intention of the three—of Divine love, of wisdom from love, and of living truth in act—so that what is received might be welcomed and remain conjoined. (Here the source text’s ending becomes fragmentary and unclear, but the sense of stable reception is preserved.)

Thus the beloved power was brought near again: the primal good that had been far off and fixed in distress. The rescuing operation entered the state of devastation and weakness and by redeeming action released it from affliction, established it in rest and joy, and made its peace enduring.

This was the first ancient turning by which wisdom sought aid, and the aid was granted.

After this, the ordered arrangement of the degrees of life was established and completed: higher and lower structures of reception were set in place; the recurring orderly motions of life were arranged; conveyances of living intelligence in elevated states were provided; the bonds that hold order together were fixed; the external planes of life with their boundaries and defenses were formed; and containing forms for uses were prepared. Thus the whole was made coherent and set into right order by heavenly goods and truths.

Then primary wisdom stood together with beloved illumination, with the forming power that orders, with the living operation of Divine truth, and with the restored primal good. These sufficient powers entered a state of united turning; they acknowledged the First Divine and sought a further provision: that a leading and guiding power might be given for all the uses they had formed, and that this power might come to cleanse the living soul still held in distress.

Their turning was received, and what they sought was granted: a new saving proceeding, a mediating manifestation of Divine operation. It came in the might of Divine greatness and surveyed the whole living soul—how it was bound by compulsions and held fast. It also perceived the ordered works established from higher states, and again perceived the living soul still chained in grievous torment, oppressed by foul delight from the deepest falsity conjoined to it.

Therefore this mediating saving operation, from love, made its manner of deliverance plain even before the deepest hellish state, in order to free the living soul. It redeemed it from deadened cravings and corporeal lusts in which it suffered, brought relief, and restored it into a state of rest and joy.

This saving mediation also fulfilled the united intention of the three, according to the request of the companion powers; thus what had been asked was given in a form suited to effect deliverance.

The third work was the removal and elevation of the living soul that had been freed: it was released from bondage, relieved of affliction, and set into a governing order, becoming primary with respect to the whole formed life.

Thus the second ancient turning has been set forth: the mediating saving operation was granted.

A third turning is introduced, but at this point the record breaks into corrupted fragments and does not yield a continuous spiritual account. Still, the remnants suggest a further manifestation of Divine truth and a concealment from those not prepared; a standing firm of what is Divine in higher states; an unveiling of light; a renewal of the primal good; contempt or mockery from opposites; an investing with outward truths; a liberation of those held; an uprising of confession and praise; and a return to united asking for release through mediating salvation.

What follows indicates conjunction of the living and the redeemed in enduring peace; a first saving separation from contraries; and the giving of hope for endurance.

Also, a more interior Divine manifestation perfected the saving intention so that the will could be ordered according to what is heavenly, and a further power of illumination and rescue was granted. The needs of lower states were answered in order and stability was established. This saving presence humbled itself so it could reach those held in opposition, and its quality was displayed even to adversaries; thus hope was received, and the light-bearing power became manifest as the granted aid for those of heaven. (Here too the source is highly broken, and the sequence can only be held in broad outline.)

And as this turning took an inward form, so too the mind is to receive within itself a stable form of order. For everyone who knows and perceives within themselves the things that flow in from a higher source—how they enter, are received, and are arranged—has within an exemplar through which stability is given.

The first effect of this saving manifestation is the redemption of the living soul bound throughout the whole ordered system of life: it is freed, cleansed, purified, and delivered through that Divine operation.

For the saving power releases the whole person who is held fast in the external self, because it proceeds from the First Divine and carries Divine pity as living efficacy. Through it redemption is made for the soul and the way of deliverance is opened; therefore there is again asking that relief be granted amid distress, and that what is sought be given for the soul that is coming out from bondage, so that it may be set into peace and brought into enduring life.

And the living soul that is freed through the aid of another soul is likewise restored in the name and quality of that person: it is purified, returned to its first essence, and becomes a fellow-helper. From that new state it also seeks aid for the one released from the external self; it desires love and the removal of evils through heavenly truths.

And as relief is given to the living soul through this cooperation, so the cooperating soul also finds relief and is delivered from the external bonds that held it. It is elevated into the state of light; and because life was restored through it, salvation is effected for it as well, and it comes into the enduring state of life and rest.

paragraph_translations.translation: When anyone who is being formed for heaven turns in full trust toward the good of love and asks for it, that asking is itself a true movement of the heart and is received by the Divine compassion. If the turning is chiefly for one’s own restoration, it is received according to that need; and if it is chiefly for another’s restoration, it is likewise received, because love looks beyond self.
paragraph_translations.connection: OPENS the chapter’s teaching on how genuine asking is received.

paragraph_translations.connection: BREAKS due to textual corruption, yet gestures toward a third phase of salvation.
paragraph_translations.notes: This paragraph is severely corrupted with disordered clauses; a continuous sequence cannot be securely recovered.

paragraph_translations.translation: Yet the remnant indicates lasting conjunction of those made living and those delivered, a first saving separation from contraries, and the giving of hope to endure.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES the fragment by extracting its stable spiritual outcomes.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Strong, continuous spiritual narrative through ¶23: genuine asking opens reception; wisdom intercedes for endangered good; saving truth rescues and orders; then a second, collective request brings a mediating saving operation that perceives bondage and purifies. Coherence weakens sharply at ¶25–¶28 due to severe textual corruption; only broad motifs can be carried through without forcing. The final paragraphs recover a clear doctrinal thread about inner formation, universal redemption, repeated asking for relief, and reciprocal salvation through mutual aid.

findings.diagnosis: Clean opening in correspondential voice: prayer/entreaty is taught by inner function (faith, charity, reception), not by a roster of powers. No narrative strain.
findings.evidence: Text teaches efficacy of prayer by what it DOES: “if he beseeches charity in total faith… he shall be favoured… if… on behalf of someone else… granted.” The spiritual reading reports no stumble and correctly derives an inner process of reception from the functional language.

findings.diagnosis: Clean continuation: the chapter frames a typological/primordial pattern (“since the beginning… first ones”) and promises to explain ‘how’ and ‘in what form’ entreaty works. This remains process-oriented and supports the narrative setup.
findings.evidence: “this entreaty has been since the beginning… gods first made entreaty… I will instruct you how… or in what form…” The spiritual reading tracks this smoothly as ‘ancient states’ and ‘form/process of reception’—no forcing required.

findings.diagnosis: Largely clean substrate narrative, but with minor administrative titulature intrusions and damaged seams inside ¶13. The core story teaches by function (intercession → sending power → rescue → rest). The reading stumbles only where the manuscript becomes fragmentary and where extra titles are stacked.
findings.evidence: Correspondential core: “she… prayed… besought… send a power; a protector and redeemer… Living Spirit… giver of ease… grasped… freed… gave him ease… land of rest.” The reading notes: “source text’s ending becomes fragmentary and unclear” at ¶13. The textual cause is visible: piled appositions and a broken clause: “the Living Spirit… [by the will of the Father and the Mother and the Living Spirit.] the Living Spirit, the first giver of ease [The Welcomer of the Lights.] the will of these three. The welcomer… [..” This reads like (a) a damaged line-break and (b) a secondary gloss-cycle of honorifics (“first giver of ease,” “Welcomer of the Lights”) that interrupts the action sequence.

findings.diagnosis: Clean but transitional: cosmological ‘building’ list is more schematic than the rescue narrative, yet it still teaches by function (structures, vessels, firmaments) and serves as narrative bridge from rescue to world-ordering. Not an insertion by itself.
findings.evidence: “they built the universe… with its firmaments, with its wheels… ships of light… fastenings… earths and its walls… vessels.” The spiritual reading treats this as “ordered arrangement… degrees of life… containing forms for uses,” and it does not report a narrative break—only a shift of topic.

findings.diagnosis: Insertion into functional narrative: a fivefold administrative roster is dropped into an otherwise correspondential sequence. The ‘five stood to prayer’ is governance/taxonomy (who stands with whom; fivefold system) rather than a functional explanation. It forces the spiritual reading to ‘render by function’ and to justify extra names that do not participate in the preceding rescue logic.
findings.evidence: The paragraph pivots from functional building (¶17) to a lineup: “The Great Spirit stood with the Beloved of the Lights, the Great Builder with the Living Spirit and the First Man. These five stood to prayer…” The reading explicitly signals strain: “Named figures beyond ‘Mother of Life/Living Spirit/First Man’ must be rendered by function; ‘Beloved of the Lights/Great Builder’ are taken as…” That is exactly the symptom of administrative material intruding: names appear as titles/jurisdictions, not as operative steps in the spiritual process. If you skip the roster clause, the narrative runs: construction (¶17) → they pray and ask for a purifier/guide (end of ¶18) → Father grants Third Ambassador (¶19).
findings.scope: Remove the roster sentence that introduces the fivefold administrative lineup: “The Great Spirit stood with the Beloved of the Lights, the Great Builder with the Living Spirit and the First Man. These five stood to prayer;”

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential unit (second entreaty): the Third Ambassador is introduced by function (perceives bondage, has compassion, reveals a way, frees, gives ease). Despite mythic naming, the passage teaches by what the saving power does, and the story flows without forcing.
findings.evidence: Functional verbs drive the teaching: “He saw… soul… entangled… had compassion… revealed his way… to free… redeemed… gave it ease… set it right… fulfilled the will… transferral… released… gave it ease.” The spiritual reading reports strong coherence through ¶23 and only notes a syntactic tangle at ¶21, not a narrative rupture.

findings.diagnosis: Damaged text (genuine difficulty), not a deliberate overlay: the paragraph is a catastrophic fragment chain with broken syntax, lost referents, and disordered snippets of multiple clauses. The reading ‘stumbles’ because there is no recoverable continuous narrative, not because of a clear administrative insertion.
findings.evidence: The text is visibly lacunose and scrambled: “displayed his image… hid his image… rulers… mock… garment… assembly… freed… their voice… the body… prayer… souls… beseech…” The spiritual reading explicitly: “record breaks into corrupted fragments… cannot be securely recovered.” Removing any one motif would not restore continuity; the whole is transmission damage.

findings.diagnosis: Clean remnant that resumes correspondential outcomes (conjunction, rest, separation from opposites, hope). It reads like a surviving summary line after the damaged ¶25.
findings.evidence: “[He joined them] with the living ones and [the redeemed ones] for ever [in rest]… [saving act]… [opposites]… hope [to endure.]” The reading successfully extracts stable outcomes and does not report voice-conflict—just compression.

findings.diagnosis: Expansion at a seam: christological identification (“Jesus the Splendour”) and systematizing will/element language are introduced into an already-broken third-entreaty context, creating a new didactic mode (naming an institutional/recognized savior figure; ordering ‘elements’) rather than continuing the chapter’s earlier prayer→aid→rescue story. The reading notes heavy breakage but also has to treat ‘Jesus the Splendour’ as a functional gloss, a classic sign of later naming at a seam.
findings.evidence: The paragraph begins with a marker of addition: “Also, Jesus the Splendour perfected the will…” and then uses administrative-systematizing diction: “the will… the elements… ordered… established… for ever,” alongside repeated re-identification: “the power that is Jesus the Splendour… Jesus the Splendour, the light power…” The spiritual reading notes: “line between ‘Jesus the Splendour’ and surrounding clauses is unclear… function is taken as interior illuminating rescue.” That is the stumble: the text supplies a named identification in a context where the narrative is otherwise fragmentary; it feels like a gloss meant to anchor doctrine rather than preserve the older story.
findings.scope: Excise the explicit christological-identificatory insertion phrase while leaving any recoverable functional clauses around it: “Also, Jesus the Splendour” (and the repeated bare identifications “the power that is Jesus the Splendour” / “Jesus the Splendour,” where they function as appositional labels rather than actions).

findings.diagnosis: Clean pivot back to correspondential instruction (inner ‘figure’ and reception). Despite fragmentation, it returns to functional teaching about an inner form/order and perception of influx. This is not administrative.
findings.evidence: “you also shall take the figure… within you… figure of order… knows… perceived… the things… within him… upon him… that flow.” The spiritual reading recognizes a clear didactic pivot to inner formation and does not report voice conflict—only lacunae.

findings.diagnosis: Clean doctrinal thesis line in correspondential voice: redemption/purification taught as effect throughout the universe. No disruption.
findings.evidence: “The first: [the redemption] of the living soul… freed and cleansed and purified and redeemed.” The spiritual reading treats it as the ‘first effect’ and the line stands independently despite the jump in paragraph numbering.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty from composite damage and minor stitching: the paragraph contains broken insertions and resumptive phrases, but the underlying correspondential thread (redeeming pity → opening way → repeated beseeching → ease and release) remains. Removing pieces does not clearly improve narrative; it is a damaged compilation of a functional exhortation.
findings.evidence: Text shows multiple ruptures: “He redeemed… entirely. He has [come from]… [And again,]… grant the entreaty… He besought… brothers… They shall make… ease…” The spiritual reading notes: “many broken insertions; the continuous spiritual thread is preserved…” That is consistent with transmission damage/stitching rather than an identifiable administrative overlay block.

findings.diagnosis: Clean closing in correspondential voice: reciprocal salvation is taught by function (a redeemed soul becomes co-helper; petitions; other soul finds ease and escapes). Despite some institutional phrasing (‘forgiveness of sins’, ‘powers of light’), the mechanism is operative and narrative-coherent.
findings.evidence: “it shall become his co-helper and beseeches… petition charity… forgiveness of sins… Just as ease has come about… this is how this soul shall find ease… goes into the land of light… rest for ever.” The spiritual reading reports regained clarity and completes the reciprocal pattern without forcing.

textual_criticism.summary: Findings: 12 total. Major disruptions: (1) ¶18 contains an administrative fivefold roster inserted into a functional narrative (recommend excise of the roster sentence). (2) ¶27 shows a seam-expansion with explicit christological identification and systematizing ‘will/elements’ diction in an already-fragmented third-entreaty context (recommend excise of the bare identification phrases). Genuine difficulties due to damage: ¶25 and ¶37 (recommend none). The rest (¶5-17, ¶19-23, ¶26, ¶28, ¶31, ¶43-44) is coherent correspondential substrate and needs no action.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: As to the question for which you ask me, the entreaty occurs and the true prayer occurs! For every elect person, if he beseeches charity in total faith, he is claiming a request from our compassionate Father. So, if he is beseeching over himself alone, he shall be favoured his entreaty; but if again he is beseeching on behalf of someone else, he shall be granted his request.
For this entreaty has been since the beginning [with the first ones, when] the gods first made entreaty of their Father. They were granted their entreaty and their request.

I will instruct you how it is that they shall beseech their entreaty from the first ones; or in what form they shall entreat their request, they who have asked for it [for the ordering of] every thing.

⟨p.272⟩ The Great Spirit, the Mother of Life, she claimed and prayed and besought and glorified and praised the first established one, who is the Father. She besought him an entreaty. She claimed of him a request. She received a great gift; she and the many powers with her.

She besought an entreaty on behalf of the First Man, because of how he had come forth and thrown himself down. He became distant from the Mother of Life. He separated from her and gave himself; in great affliction. He joined war on earth with the destruction and the grief and the weakness; in the worlds of darkness; in the abysses made of fear; in the midst of the demons' ditch; amongst the powers of the devil!

Indeed, he is like a king standing in the midst of his enemies. And when the Mother of Life petitioned and prayed and glorified and praised the Father, the first established one, she did petition him that he might send a power; a protector and redeemer and helper for the son of God who is set in affliction.

⟨p.273⟩ Now, just as she had besought and interceded, so likewise was her prayer fulfilled and received into the presence of the Father of Greatness. He turned and gave to her her entreaty: the great power, the Living Spirit, the giver of ease. The Mother of Life and the Living Spirit came with great power to the borders of the territory. They brought the First Man up from that war and struggle, wherein he is set.

He gave himself as a grace for the Mother of Life. He became estranged and far from her, the one whom his enemies (place) in great affliction, the one who is in the land of darkness since he became weak.

The Living Spirit grasped and took him in. He freed him. He set him right and gave him ease in the land of rest [by the will of the Father and the Mother and the Living Spirit.] the Living Spirit, the first giver of ease [The Welcomer of the Lights.] the will of these three. The welcomer [the living soul that is brought up from the war may remain in its place of rest.] find with the welcomer that [...

[And then she brought near again] a great power [and she clothed him] of the loved one [the power] the First Man who had been far away. He had become distant. She had besought on his behalf. He was set fast in affliction. (The Living Spirit) went to the place of destruction and weakness, the one that freed and redeemed him and gave him ease from the affliction. He set him right with rest and joy. He has himself become rested, with him for ever.
See now, I have taught you the first entreaty that the Mother of Life besought by her prayer. They granted her her entreaty.

[Then they took counsel together] and they built the universe and completed it with its firmaments, with its wheels, with the ships of light that are in the heights, with its fastenings, with its earths and its walls, with its vessels. They completed the universe and set it right by the fathers of light.

They glorified and praised the Father, the first established one. They besought of him an entreaty. They claimed of him a request, that he might give them the power [of the purifier,] the leader, a guide to all the things of activity that they had constructed. That he might come and purify the living soul that is set in affliction.
